(:2686 verbatim) with Reclaim the blessed third word (owner ruling 2026-10-17, ADR-0017 #1; isolate stayed dbaas's under the card's own rider :2687, expire stayed a law). Census: 66 templates — decision 37 / flavour 29, zero era objects (bundle availableFrom null; §0.4 dates no CI cell). The shared register — refusal 5, status ladder 5, vendor canon 4 — is byte-identical across all fourteen packs (validator law); the line's own voices carry the board: green squares, held runners, the queue wall, the secret the board cannot print (:2684, :2704). §9.11 business-not-technique holds throughout: the fatal leak, the fork storm, and the poisoned cache are told as CONSEQUENCES with no commands, no payload shapes, and no credential text.

decision.type.ci-build-farm.name: Green Light
decision.type.ci-build-farm.codex: You sell the execution of arbitrary code written by strangers — 'That is not a bug in the product; it is the product.' (:2678-2679). The board is a wall of green and red squares, 'the most instantly readable board in the game, and it's real' (:2704); real and sufficient are different words. The fastest floor is the dirty floor: 'reused is fast and a cross-tenant contamination vector; ephemeral is safe and cold' (:2691-2692), and the §6.12 Kite card sells the same margin 'with the right to reclaim it' (:22235). 'The fast path and the safe path are opposites' (§1.9 :5061).
decision.goal.ci-build-farm.binding: Warmth and cleanliness, never both: the queue wall decides what Monday can promise while the hygiene dial decides what Thursday can leak — 'developers tolerate slow builds and not queued builds' (:2689-2690 verbatim), and every runner still warm is a secret still reachable. The bound is not the minutes you sell; it is the overhead you can't bill ('pure overhead you can't bill for', :2683) — the quarter is held at the seam between fast+unsafe and safe+cold (:2691-2692), and the wall's honesty is the product you cannot afford to spend.
decision.scarce.ci-build-farm.qos: Queue position before queue speed: a build that waits honestly in line is a promise kept, a build silently reordered past the wall is the product broken — 'Queue depth is the only metric anyone looks at' (:2689 verbatim) and the ladder sheds strictly by the truth of the line, never by the wealth of the plan. Warmth is rationed second: the cache stays or the cold start pays, the dial chooses who eats ('how much dependency cache you keep warm', :2681-2682).
decision.skin.ci-build-farm.inspector: The status wall, crate rows flushing under it. Inspect a runner and the drawer is honest in two directions: the percentage genuinely fresh vs 'reused because we were busy' (:2702-2703 verbatim core), the cache it carries, the credential tag still clipped to its frame (:2685), and the last job that died on it — because on this floor the inspector is the hygiene report, and the hygiene report is the notice channel the fatality walks in through.
decision.economy.ci-build-farm.bad-month: The month the wall stayed green. A free-tier job reaches sideways through a warm runner's seam into another tenant's cache and out (:2700), a fork-PR build runs attacker code with borrowed production credentials (:2699), and the postmortems are everyone's at once — 'a customer whose secrets leak into a public build log' (:2700 verbatim) is the sentence that ends engineering-team accounts, because the credentials were 'for every customer' (:2685). Companion C prices no row for this line; the month is composed from the card's own columns, and the absence is on record.
decision.cac.ci-build-farm.platform-slot-cycle: The platform 'recommended' slot is the doc's verdict in its own column headers: a channel 'Political + engineering', a sales cycle of '12+ months', power '**Highest**', fragility 'Fragile (they can remove you)', capacity 'One slot', and the table's closing judgement, 'Best channel in hosting' (:13417 verbatim census). Engineering teams do not search for farms; they arrive pre-blessed by the marketplace their CTO already trusts — one slot, twelve months of courting, and a churn switch you did not install.
decision.verbs.ci-build-farm.transfer.1: The fast path and the safe path are opposites.
decision.relations.ci-build-farm.mastery: Mastery on this floor is the reflex the automation ladder warns you into: 'Each step converts toil into capex plus blast radius' (§5.6 :20671-20672 verbatim core). The player stops asking 'is it green?' and starts asking 'would I run THAT commit on a runner that held my bank's keys?' — warm or ephemeral becomes a felt temperature, the reclaim cadence becomes muscle memory, and the Monday Wall stops being a surprise and starts being a budget line.
decision.relations.ci-build-farm.distillate: Destroy-on-release, distilled: any floor that lets tenants touch one shared thing inherits this line's reflex — the runner is a secret holder between jobs (:2685), and hygiene is not a report but a cadence. The science travels wherever strangers' code runs: shared kernels, shared caches, shared desks; the wall of squares stays behind as the cheapest honest UI in the game.
decision.handover.ci-build-farm.runs-out: Clean ephemeral capacity and the queue's honesty. Their speed is your capacity plan: one push fans {jobCount} crates across the fleet, the Monday Wall lands at the week's first hour with the farm sized for the weekend's silence (:2694), and the limiter that saves the boundary eats the warmth they are paying you for — 'ephemeral is safe and cold' (:2692 verbatim), a Friction tower by design.
decision.handover.ci-build-farm.kills-you: The leak (§1.4 verbatim fatality): a secret crossing a tenant boundary inside a runner that was reused because someone was busy — 'a leaked secret between tenants' builds, because CI runners hold production credentials for every customer' — the one catastrophe where the board never turns red, because the board is honest about jobs and blind about seams (:2684-2685).
decision.handover.ci-build-farm.customer-wants: Green, and soon: 'engineering teams, who feel every second' (:2685 verbatim), whose patience the tuning spine already priced — 'patient, but value decays with queue time' (:11975) — and whose trust is the wall itself: they tolerate the slow build and never the queued one, and they will leave a farm that leaks once faster than one that queues twice.
decision.rosetta.ci-build-farm.warmth: Preemptible warmth is the oversell ratio wearing a kite's tail: shared-web sells slots against a bet that tenants under-use them; this line sells the WARM margin against a bet that nobody leaks — 'Monetizes idle capacity at a discount, with the right to reclaim it … which is exactly the trap the game wants you to consider' (§6.12 spot/preemptible card verbatim, :22234-22238). The reclaim clause is the doc's own word and the door's own verb: the string that can be cut at any moment runs through your own fleet.
decision.rosetta.ci-build-farm.caging: The queue-depth ceiling is cgroup-caging taught by the wall: 'one tenant's silent excess is everyone's queue' arrives here as a monorepo needing 400GB of cache (:2701 verbatim core) instead of a noisy neighbor eating IOPS — the cabling is identical, the meter is the line outside, and the shed must never lie about either.
decision.scenarios.ci-build-farm.wall-goes-red: A bad dependency propagates across the fleet while the board flushes red square by square, left to right, in publish order (:2705) — the most legible catastrophe in the game, told by furniture that cannot lie about what it can see.
decision.scenarios.ci-build-farm.fork-until-it-di: A build arrives that multiplies instead of compiles; the host spends its slots on its own grandchildren and falls over (:2699) — consequence told, method never; the grudge is the payload.
decision.scenarios.ci-build-farm.secret-in-the-lo: A green build publishes a public log that carries another tenant's credential label (:2700) — the incident the wall cannot show, the ticket that opens three enterprise churns, the reason destroy-on-release is a product feature and not a hygiene blog post.
decision.alert.queue-wall-rising: Queue depth {queueDepth} and climbing at {hour} local — the wall is filling left to right.
decision.alert.runner-reused-flag: Runner hygiene at {reusedPct}% reused — {runnerName} came back from a job it should not have kept.
decision.alert.cache-poison-suspected: Cache-integrity check failed on {repoName}: the artifact seeded at build {day} predates the merge that produced it.
decision.alert.monday-wall-landed: The Monday Morning Wall landed: {jobCount} jobs from the weekend's pushes queued inside the first hour.
decision.alert.secret-boundary-crossed: A build for {repoName} printed {secretName} into a log another tenant can read. The wall is still green.
decision.terms.warm-ephemeral: The minute price is a temperature: warm minutes bill fast and cold minutes bill clean. You can sell the margin; the string can be cut at any moment.
decision.terms.cache-retention: Cached dependency sets persist between builds on reused runners. Bigger vaults, faster Mondays, wider seams — the dial has no middle position.
decision.terms.flaky-report: The flakiness report is sold as a product and paid for as a discount on the tax: their re-runs are your load, and both sides prefer the sentence that way.
decision.refusal.hands-exhausted: Both hands are committed. The {verb} intent is queued and presents when a hand frees at tick {availableAtTick}.
decision.refusal.stamped-in-future: The {verb} intent is stamped for tick {availableAtTick}, ahead of the current minute. Nothing was spent.
decision.refusal.unknown-node: No board object named {nodeId} exists at the current tick. Nothing was changed.
decision.refusal.edge-exists: A {relationKind} cable already links {nodeId} to those endpoints. The existing edge was left as it is.
decision.refusal.slot-occupied: {slotName} on {nodeId} is occupied. One supplier per socket; disconnect before you reconnect.
decision.status.rung-5: We are aware of the fire.

flavour.ticket.subject.queue-depth: why is my build at {queueDepth} deep since {hour} local
flavour.ticket.body.queue-depth: It has been green-in-principle for two hours. The wall says queued, my pipeline says waiting, my manager says demo at nine. — {customerName}, ticket {ticketId}
flavour.ticket.subject.flaky-tax: re-ran the red build {flakyRate} times, still red, still your fault
flavour.ticket.body.flaky-tax: Your runner ate my artifact cache overnight and now every test I own is 'flaky' on the dashboard. If the re-runs cost you minutes, charge me for the honesty instead. — {customerName}, ticket {ticketId}
flavour.ticket.subject.secret-scare: is {secretName} supposed to appear in a PUBLIC log
flavour.ticket.body.secret-scare: Our contractor's build just printed a label that matches our deploy credential. Please tell me it is a name and not a value. Please tell me now. — {customerName}, ticket {ticketId}
flavour.press.headline.green: The Most Readable Board In Hosting: Inside The Wall Of Squares That Runs The Week
flavour.press.headline.leaked: Green Until Thursday: Tenants Say Farm Leak Stayed Invisible On The Wall That 'Cannot Lie'
flavour.forum.thread.matrix: PSA: one push fanned {jobCount} jobs and ate the whole pool — farm limits your concurrency, you don't limit it
flavour.forum.thread.cache: My monorepo cache is {cacheSizeGb} GB now. The warm plan pays for itself and I hate that it does.
flavour.chatter.desk.wall: 'Slow is fine. Queued is not.' — the whole desk knows the sentence by hour three of Monday.
flavour.chatter.runner.hum: The fans never stop. The jobs end, the runners stay warm, and nobody bills a warm one.
flavour.codex.wall: The status wall is the game's honest instrument: every square reports exactly one job's truth. The catastrophes on this floor are the ones no square holds — the seam between tenants, the secret in the log, the reuse nobody audited.
flavour.codex.hygiene: Runner hygiene is the percentage genuinely fresh versus 'reused because we were busy.' The number is the level: at 0% you are cold and safe, at 100% you are fast and one log line from a company-ending ticket.
flavour.loading.tip.queue: Queue depth is the only metric anyone looks at. The dashboard has exactly one number for a reason.
flavour.loading.tip.ephemeral: Ephemeral is safe and cold. Reused is fast and shared. The dial between them has a name: your incident log.
flavour.intern.entry.firstday: Day one. Learned the board: green means the strangers' code agreed with itself today. Asked what it means when it leaks. Nobody looked up.
flavour.intern.entry.reboot: Week two. The weekend reclaim runs while the farm is empty — destroy everything, pay the cold start Monday, sleep anyway. They call it hygiene week. It is the only quiet week.
flavour.sticky.note.window: Freeze the fleet before the weekend: the dead-quiet is the only hour the destroy-everything cadence is affordable.
flavour.abuse.canon.free: The free tier is not a marketing budget here; it is the quarry. The most abused free product in the industry mines on our clocks and prints green doing it.
flavour.abuse.canon.miner: Plan {planName}, job silent, fan loud: the crate compiles nothing and earns everything. The counter is the destroyer, and the destroyer is billed by the minute.
flavour.vendor.reply.firmware: Have you tried updating to the latest firmware?
flavour.vendor.reply.known-issue: This is a known issue, fixed in the next release (no ETA).
flavour.vendor.reply.log-bundle: Please collect a full log bundle.
flavour.achievement.wall-held: The Wall Held — one quarter, one sawtooth, zero silent squares
flavour.achievement.weekend-clean: Hygiene Week — reclaimed the fleet over a dead weekend and paid only cold
flavour.achievement.zero-leak: Strangers Stay Strangers — a quarter of arbitrary code with every boundary intact
flavour.canary.badge-tally: The status badge on the README is this floor's canary: external, deliberately primitive, and the first thing every team checks when the wall itself starts to look optimistic.
